coherence_issues.description: While the summary details various profitability metrics (net loss, operating profit, EBITDA) and their adjustments, it does not explicitly clarify the relationship between these metrics and the stated 'core operational business generating positive cash flow.' The logical bridge between adjusted EBITDA positivity and operational cash flow generation could be more explicitly articulated.

candidate_sentences.text: Despite this strong top-line growth, the Group reported a net loss for the year of SEK 125,799 thousand, resulting in earnings per share of SEK -35.29, an improvement from the SEK -29.00 loss per share in 2024.
The Group’s operating profit improved significantly to -29,270 thousand SEK from -51,781 thousand SEK in the prior year.
EBITDA turned positive at 2,957 thousand SEK, a stark contrast to the -28,229 thousand SEK reported in 2024.

When adjusted for one-off costs of approximately 10,238 thousand SEK related to the liquidation of older company structures, the adjusted EBITDA amounted to approximately 13,195 thousand SEK, representing an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 32 percent of revenue.

details.coherence_justification: The summary is generally coherent with a clear narrative about OODA AI AB's 2025 financial transformation. It logically connects revenue growth to major contract invoicing (S2-S3), explains the net loss through financial impairments (S4-S5, S11-S12), and details operational improvements via operating profit and EBITDA (S6-S9). Capital raising and liquidity improvements are also clearly presented (S15-S16). However, there is a minor logical gap in how adjusted EBITDA positivity translates to operational cash flow generation, as the connection between these metrics isn't explicitly explained, leaving a small gap in the logical flow.
